For nearly 25 years, APD Global has set the benchmark in delivering advanced, comprehensive, and specialised engineering solutions.

We have around 800 employees including our alliance contracting partners, across 15 strategically located offices in Australia (Perth, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide, Darwin), New Zealand and Malaysia. We specialise in seamless integration across the Power Systems, Telecommunications, and Renewable Energy industries. Our expertise spans Power Systems Studies, Transmission Lines, Substations, Telecommunications, Protection, Control & Automation, Renewable Energy Connections, Mining, and Engineering, Protection Panel Design and Installation, 3D Design and Manufacturing as well as Construction/Management (EPC/M) services.

We have outstanding opportunity for an experienced Telecommunications Technologist to join and bring their expertise, integrity, and a positive can-do attitude to our dedicated team of professionals.

Position Overview
The Telecommunications Technologist is responsible for designing, implementing, maintaining, and troubleshooting telecommunications systems and networks. This position ensures the reliable operation of voice, data, and video communications across the organisation, supporting both internal and external connectivity requirements.

Key Responsibilities
Install, configure, and maintain telecommunications equipment and systems, including routers, switches, fiber optic cables, PBX, VoIP, and wireless technologies
Installing routers, switches, fiber optic cables, and telephone systems
Monitor and optimise the performance of telecommunications networks and troubleshoot issues to ensure optimal operation and minimal downtime
Collaborate with IT and other departments to integrate telecommunications solutions that meet business needs
Conduct tests and measurements on telecommunications equipment and networks
Conduct regular system upgrades and apply security protocols to safeguard communications infrastructure and ensuring compliance with safety standards
Provide technical support and training to end-users regarding telecommunications equipment and services
Document system configurations, network diagrams, maintenance repairs, and procedures for ongoing reference and compliance
Stay up-to-date with emerging technologies and industry best practices

Key Selection Criteria
Relevant tertiary qualifications in telecommunications, information technology, or a related field
Proven experience in managing and maintaining telecommunications networks and systems
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to resolve complex technical issues
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a customer-focused approach
Knowledge of Australian telecommunications standards and regulatory requirements

Desirable Attributes
Experience with cloud-based communications platforms
Ability to work independently and as part of a team
Strong organisational skills and attention to detail

If you have the skills required for this role and you feel this is the job for you, then apply now!

About the Business
Robust IT Services is a dynamic and growing IT solutions provider based in South Geelong, specialising in managed IT services, infrastructure design, cloud solutions, network security, vulnerability testing, data security, and comprehensive business IT support. With a strong focus on delivering responsive, reliable, and forward-thinking technological solutions, the company has built a solid reputation for helping businesses of all sizes optimise their IT environments, mitigate risks, and drive operational success. Guided by values of innovation, quality, professionalism, and customer-centric service, Robust IT fosters a collaborative, supportive workplace culture where team members are encouraged to solve challenges, continuously develop their skills, and contribute to meaningful client outcomes in a fast-paced yet balanced environment.
About the Position
The ICT Support Technician plays a key hands-on role within Robust IT Services by providing day-to-day technical support to end-users and clients, diagnosing and resolving hardware, software, and network issues, and ensuring the reliable operation of IT systems and infrastructure. This position is essential for maintaining high service standards, minimising downtime, and delivering excellent customer support across the company’s internal operations and client environments.
Key Responsibilities
Provide timely technical support and assistance to end-users, diagnosing and resolving hardware, software, network, and peripheral issues.
Install, configure, maintain, and upgrade computer systems, operating systems, applications, and network components.
Respond to user inquiries about IT problems and provide clear guidance and solutions.
Manage user accounts, permissions, and access in systems such as Active Directory and Microsoft 365.
Perform regular system backups, updates, patches, and basic security maintenance.
Troubleshoot and resolve issues with printers, mobile devices, and other peripherals.
Maintain accurate documentation of support activities, procedures, and asset records.
Collaborate with the team on IT projects, system improvements, and client support initiatives.

Requirements
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Diploma in Information Technology or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
Minimum 1 year of experience in IT support, helpdesk, or a similar technical role.
Strong technical skills in troubleshooting hardware and software issues, Microsoft environments (including Office 365 and Active Directory), networking fundamentals, and remote support tools.
Excellent customer service, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical users.
Ability to work independently and as part of a small team in a fast-paced environment.

To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.

The primary purpose of the role is to provide effective clinical management of surgical patients in the clinical Eastern and Greater Southern Surgical Skills Network. Unaccredited Trainee rotations will be based at St Vincent's Hospitals and occur at the following hospitals:

Trauma Surgery-Acute Surgical Unit, SVH

Cardiothoracic Surgery, SVH

St Vincent's Health Network Sydney (SVHN) forms part of the NSW region of St Vincent's Health Australia which is the largest diversified health care organisation within Australia's not for profit and Catholic health care sectors. SVHN comprises some of Australia's oldest and most prestigious hospitals; these include St Vincent's Hospital and Sacred Heart Hospice. Along with three co-located research institutes - the Victor Chang Cardiac Research Institute, the Garvan Institute of Medical Research, and St Vincent's Institute of Medical Research - we work in close partnership with other research bodies, universities, and health care providers.

St. Vincents Hospital is a major public hospital and a principal tertiary referral hospital. St Vincents specialises in heart-lung transplantation; bone marrow transplantation; cardiology; neurosurgery, cancer; clinical genomics, HIV medicine; palliative care, respiratory medicine; mental health; and drug and alcohol services, aged psychiatry, homeless health and prisoner health. We are a clinical and education leader with a national and international reputation in medical research

Centrally located in Darlinghurst, it sits on the edge of Sydney's business district. St. Vincents follows the philosophy of the Mary Aikenhead Ministries in its service to all regardless of race, nationality or creed. St Vincent's Health Australia provides compassionate healthcare to people from all walks of life, but reflecting our mission, we are especially committed to people from vulnerable and marginalised backgrounds.

The Hospital has a long-standing reputation for treating the highest acuity and complex patient loads, attracting referrals on a state-wide and national basis. The Hospital is a teaching hospital of the UNSW and University of Notre Dame and has academic associations with the Australian Catholic University, Sydney University and the University of Technology, Sydney.

result.description: Recruitment Links Australia  We are seeking an experienced Project Administrator to coordinate and support the delivery of civil, structural, and installation works. Working closely with management, schedulers, site supervisors, field teams, contractors and clients, you will maintain project records, monitor work progress, coordinate resources and provide accurate operational reporting. This is a hands-on administration role requiring strong organisation, commercial awareness and the ability to manage multiple active projects and competing deadlines. The role is primarily based in South Lismore NSW, but you may also work in Sydney depending on project needs.   Benefits  Salary range: $80,000 - $90,000 per Annum + Superannuation.   Task & responsibilities   Providing project administration support across civil, structural, and installation works.   Coordinating documentation, scheduling, reporting, and delivery tracking across concurrent projects.   Leveraging existing industry relationships to identify and support new business development opportunities, particularly in steel fabrication and installation works.   Monitor project progress against schedules, identify delays or service issues and escalate matters requiring management attention.   Assist management with process improvements, project reviews, compliance documentation and implementation of operational decisions.   Supporting tender preparation, RFP/RFQ responses, scope definition, and construction methodology development.   Liaising with clients, subcontractors, councils, and authorities to coordinate approvals and inspections.   Assisting with WHS documentation, QA checklists, and handover packs.  Contributing to the growth of the Sydney project portfolio through relationship development and opportunity identification.    Qualification & experience   At least 3 years of highly relevant experience in project administration, construction operations, logistics or a comparable service-based environment.   Demonstrated experience coordinating multiple projects, work orders, schedules and operational stakeholders.   Strong written communication, reporting, document-control and record-management skills.  Ability to interpret project requirements, identify priorities and follow through on actions within required timeframes.   Effective problem-solving skills and the ability to work calmly in a fast-paced operational environment.   Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate professionally with clients, site supervisors, contractors and internal teams.   About Company    MESI Group is a proudly Australian-owned and operated company, committed to maintaining the highest safety standards and attention to detail, ensuring top-quality solutions for our clients across all projects. We specialise in designing, supplying, and installing Guyed Masts, Lattice Towers, structural solutions and custom-designed structures. Australia Network Services PTY LTD is hiring a Full-time Business Analyst role in Strathfield, NSW. Apply now to be part of our team.

Requirements for this role:

Flexible hours available

2-3 years of relevant work experience required for this role

AUSTRALIA NETWORK SERVICES PTY LTD is looking for an experienced Business Analyst for our client’s ICT and business systems operations in Sydney. On a full-time basis, you will be part of a multidisciplinary and well-supported team.

Title: Business Analyst, Full-time position

Salary: A$90,000.00 to A$98,000.00 plus super

Work Location: In person.

We are looking for applicants who demonstrate the following:



Requirements

- Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in business analysis, ICT systems support, or business systems operations
- Relevant qualification in Information Systems, Business Information Systems, Computer Science, Information Technology, or equivalent
- Strong understanding of business processes, system workflows, and operational requirements
- Experience gathering, analysing, and documenting business and system requirements
- Experience with Microsoft 365, Active Directory, ServiceNow, Google Workspace, or similar business systems
- Ability to prepare process documentation, user guides, operational reports, and system support materials
- Strong stakeholder communication skills and ability to work with both technical and non-technical users
- Good analytical, problem-solving, and organisational skills
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy and system improvement
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team

Responsibilities

- Analyse existing business processes, ICT workflows, and operational systems to identify inefficiencies and areas for improvement.
- Consult with internal users, clients, and stakeholders to understand business needs and translate them into clear functional system requirements.
- Prepare business requirement documents, workflow diagrams, process notes, user guides, and system documentation.
- Work closely with developers, IT support teams, and business users to ensure system requirements are clearly understood and properly implemented.
- Support system testing, user acceptance testing, issue tracking, and implementation of business system improvements.
- Review and improve user access workflows, account management processes, shared drive structures, permission controls, and business application procedures.
- Prepare operational reports, maintain accurate system records, and support data integrity across business platforms.
- Assist with onboarding and offboarding processes, staff training, and system usage guidance for business users.
- Monitor business system performance, user issues, and service requests to support reliable day-to-day operations.
- Maintain clear communication with stakeholders and provide practical solutions to improve business efficiency and system usability.
- If you would like to discuss the role further, please click APPLY and send through an up-to-date CV. We can schedule a time to discuss the position available and what will be best suited to you.
